claim: The rule that a payment draft has received_amount equal to paid_amount (one currency on both sides) is written separately in the create body, in the update body and in the currency warning. If a maintainer changes how create sets received_amount, update would keep writing the old rule onto the same drafts, and the warning would describe the old rule.
evidence: bank_and_cash.py create_draft_payment_entry: `# One currency on both sides: ERPNext wants both amounts before it counts them.` / `"paid_amount": inputs.paid_amount,` / `"received_amount": inputs.paid_amount,`; update_draft_payment_entry: `if inputs.paid_amount is not None: doc |= {"paid_amount": inputs.paid_amount, "received_amount": inputs.paid_amount}`; _payment_warnings: `"... the draft's received_amount equals paid_amount and its exchange rates may not match ..."`. Suppose create is changed so that received_amount comes from the bank account's currency, for example to drop the mismatch warning. An update_draft_payment_entry that only changes paid_amount still sends received_amount = paid_amount. The draft then holds two different rules depending on whether it was last created or updated, and the warning text is stale for both.
proposal: Test: create a payment draft, update only paid_amount, and assert that the bodies sent on create and on update set received_amount by the same rule (fake ERPNext records both bodies). Change: add one helper, e.g. `def _amounts(paid: Decimal) -> dict[str, Decimal]: return {"paid_amount": paid, "received_amount": paid}`, and call it from both create and update, with the comment kept beside it. The warning text in _payment_warnings can then cite that helper's rule.

verdict.reproduction: Create: src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:513-515 `# One currency on both sides: ERPNext wants both amounts before it counts them.` / `"paid_amount": inputs.paid_amount,` / `"received_amount": inputs.paid_amount,`. Update: src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:570-571 `if inputs.paid_amount is not None: doc |= {"paid_amount": inputs.paid_amount, "received_amount": inputs.paid_amount}`. Warning: src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:466-469 `"... the draft's received_amount equals paid_amount and its exchange rates may not match the accounts..."`. The tests already pin each copy: tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash_drafts.py:151 and :196 (create bodies asserted exactly, `"received_amount": 119` with `"paid_amount": 119`), :596 and :739 (update bodies asserted exactly, `"received_amount": 100`/`50` with the same paid_amount), tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:631. Nothing was run; reading the code and tests was enough.
verdict.reason: The rule really is written in three places: create (bank_and_cash.py:513-515), update (:570-571) and the currency warning (:466-469). But it is a drop. (1) It is not a free choice a maintainer would change in one place. The spec requires it: docs/specs/req-007-*.md REQ-007-PRS-F004's Definition of Done says a create sends "`received_amount` equal to `paid_amount`". Changing create to use the bank account's currency would mean changing the spec first, and that change would cover update and the warning too. (2) The tests already hold the copies equal. Exact-body assertions for create (tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash_drafts.py:151, :196) and for update (:596, :739) fail if either side changes alone. The task's rule says copies the tests already hold equal are a drop. (3) Nobody acts wrongly today: create and update write the same rule, and the warning describes that rule correctly. A helper would add indirection that protects nothing the tests don't already catch.

claim: The kind of journal entry Enterich creates and the kind it accepts for an update are written as two separate literals. If a maintainer changes what create writes, update refuses the agent's own new drafts. The payment side avoids this by building both from SIDES.
evidence: record_to_report.py create_draft_journal_entry: `{**doc, "voucher_type": "Journal Entry", "multi_currency": 0}`; update_draft_journal_entry: `only=({"voucher_type": "Journal Entry"},), kind="a journal entry of voucher type Journal Entry"` and `if stored.get("multi_currency"): raise Refusal(...)`. Compare bank_and_cash.py update_draft_payment_entry: `only=[{"payment_type": side.payment_type, "party_type": party_type} for party_type, side in SIDES.items()]`, the same SIDES that create uses. Suppose create starts writing voucher_type "Bank Entry" when cheque_no is given. The next update_draft_journal_entry on that draft is refused with `name: ... isn't a journal entry of voucher type Journal Entry, the only kind Enterich changes`, even though Enterich made the draft itself.
proposal: Test: for each body create_draft_journal_entry inserts, assert that drafts.editable's `only` accepts the stored draft (fake ERPNext returns the inserted body as stored). Change: define `JOURNAL_KIND = {"voucher_type": "Journal Entry", "multi_currency": 0}` once. Create sends `{**doc, **JOURNAL_KIND}`, update passes `only=({"voucher_type": JOURNAL_KIND["voucher_type"]},)`, and the update's kind text and multi_currency refusal are built from the same constant.

verdict.reason: The two literals are real: record_to_report.py:593 creates with `{**doc, "voucher_type": "Journal Entry", "multi_currency": 0}`, and record_to_report.py:610-613 updates with `only=({"voucher_type": "Journal Entry"},)` and refuses `multi_currency`. But the value is not one a maintainer can change in one place. The spec sets it for both operations. docs/specs/req-006-*.md:106 (REQ-006-PRS-F006 area / F005) says update refuses "a draft whose voucher type isn't Journal Entry" and any draft with `multi_currency` set. The catalogue row at line 192 says create sends "`voucher_type` Journal Entry; `multi_currency` 0". The finding's scenario (create writes "Bank Entry" when cheque_no is given) would therefore be a spec change. It is ruled out by the contract, not something left behind by accident. The tests already tie the copies. tests/integration/test_record_to_report_drafts.py:123-124 and :140-141 pin the create body to voucher_type "Journal Entry" and multi_currency 0. Lines :525 and :555 pin the update refusals. tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:435 creates a journal entry and then updates it with update_draft_journal_entry, so an update refusing the agent's own draft would fail there. Changing create alone fails these tests. Copies the tests already hold equal, and a value the spec fixes, are a drop by the lens's own bar. The constant the finding proposes would add indirection and protect nothing.

claim: Which of a party's and an invoice's fields are yes/no fields is written twice for each, once for the list and once for the get, as literals outside Side. A Check field added to Side's party_fields or invoice_fields and flagged in only one place comes back as true/false from one operation and as 0/1 from the other.
evidence: invoicing.py _party: `shape(doc, side.party_fields, outside=side.party_outside, flags={"disabled"})`; get_party: `shape(doc, (*side.party_fields, "payment_terms"), outside=side.party_outside, flags={"disabled"})`; _invoice: `shape(doc, side.invoice_fields, outside=side.invoice_outside, flags={"is_return"})`; get_invoice: `get_document(..., fields=(*side.invoice_fields, *INVOICE_DETAIL_FIELDS), outside=side.invoice_outside, flags={"is_return"}, ...)`. Outside text is part of Side (`party_outside`, `invoice_outside`), so it has one source; the flags are not. Suppose a maintainer adds `on_hold` to PURCHASE.invoice_fields and to _invoice's flags. list_purchase_invoices then returns `on_hold: true`, while get_purchase_invoice returns `on_hold: 1`, against REQ-001's Results rule that yes/no fields are true and false. A field that exists on only one side can't go into the shared literal at all.
proposal: Test: for each Side, assert that the yes/no fields of list_* and get_* results for a party and for an invoice are the same set, and that every one is a bool. Change: add `party_flags` and `invoice_flags` (frozenset) to invoicing.Side, set them in SALES and PURCHASE, and pass `flags=side.party_flags` and `flags=side.invoice_flags` in _party, get_party, _invoice and get_invoice.

verdict.reproduction: Each yes/no set is written twice in src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py, outside Side. Party: line 107, in `_party`, which list_parties uses: `shape(doc, side.party_fields, outside=side.party_outside, flags={"disabled"})`. Lines 153-154, in get_party: `shape(doc, (*side.party_fields, "payment_terms"), outside=side.party_outside, flags={"disabled"})`. Invoice: line 111, in `_invoice`, which list_invoices uses: `shape(doc, side.invoice_fields, outside=side.invoice_outside, flags={"is_return"})`. Lines 256-258, in get_invoice: `fields=(*side.invoice_fields, *INVOICE_DETAIL_FIELDS), outside=side.invoice_outside, flags={"is_return"}`. src/enterich/shapes.py:158 turns a field to bool only if it is in `flags`, so a Check field added to Side.invoice_fields and flagged in only one place would come back as 0/1 from the other operation.
verdict.reason: The duplication is real, and the outside text, unlike the flags, does come from Side (invoicing.py:79-95). But it is a drop because nobody acts wrongly today. Both copies hold the same set now ({"disabled"}, {"is_return"}), and every field in party_fields and invoice_fields that should be flagged is flagged. The integration tests already hold the list and get copies equal by checking types. tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:124 checks `{type(r["disabled"]) for r in every} == {bool}` for the list, and :176 checks `type(result["disabled"]) is bool` for the get. :309 and :391 check that is_return is False in the list and in the get, and test_procure_to_pay.py:272 does the same for the purchase side. The risk is only a future maintainer who adds a Check field. Under AGENTS.md's spec-first and tests-first rules, that change comes with a spec line and tests for each operation's result. The proposed change adds two Side fields to each of SALES and PURCHASE, which is more machinery than this hypothetical slip warrants. None of the listed patterns fits: no field is compared with ==, and no argument sent to ERPNext is dropped.
